steps.name: Ægir Researcher A
steps.text: Based on geological conditions, it's a promising volcano, but the location is less than optimal.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher A
steps.text: It would be difficult to establish a lengthy energy transportation pipeline while fending off Seaborn attacks.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: Did you read the Academy of Technology's report?

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: Hydrogen from seawater can be used to maintain operation of the Legion fleet, but it would be difficult to guarantee uninterrupted energy supply to the beacon.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: It alone accounts for half of the entire city's energy consumption.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher A
steps.text: It used to be much worse. Our ancestors had to design a bio-energy system for it, maintained through the joint effort of a dozen cities.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher A
steps.text: In this day and age, a system like that would be attacked by the Seaborn before it could even be activated.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: Regardless, we need to find a way to ensure power supply for the beacon.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher A
steps.text: Maybe Appius would know a way. Let me get in... oh!

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: Did you forget? He's still in the home territories and our cities are under radio silence.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: We can't exactly lay fiber optic cables like we used to, either, what with all the Seaborn out there.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher A
steps.text: I miss the days when we could get anyone in the country on a holographic call whenever we wanted.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Ægir Researcher B
steps.text: What if we modified the output mode of the energy converter?

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: We have extremely limited experience in this area. There's always a safety risk.

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: With you in charge of the cognitive link, I believe the risk is reasonable.

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: Well, I'm glad you're that confident in me, but I'm not. Who knows what an extended conversation via cognitive link with our transformed countrymen would do to both our minds?

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: There's been plenty of research into this. We'll be good as long as you keep a steady hand.

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: Even in the home territories, there are very few cases of transformed citizens being granted a final interview. Most are simply euthanized.

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: Consul Clementia's ideas are radical, as always.

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: Which is exactly why I followed her here.

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: By sorting through the threads of reason via conversation, we can grant them a chance to leave a final trace of their sapience in the world.

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: And what better way to send them off than with a stimulating debate?

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: Sadly, most of the survivors the Sea Patrol brings back are already transformed beyond recognition. Precious few have the opportunity to return to the city to receive a final interview.

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: Say—

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: We're witnessing history unfold here, aren't we?

steps.name: Ægir Scholar
steps.text: Or maybe we're just doing our jobs. I trust that the Institute of Development Planning's faith in you is not misplaced. Make your preparations.

steps.name: Ægir Doctor
steps.text: Thanks. See you in the isolation chamber.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Excuse me—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: W-What the? A Catastrophe? Under the sea?
Taken by surprise, the young man loses balance and falls, but an even stranger sight stifles his cry of surprise—
He sees the passersby float into the air, swimming through it like fins through water, paying little heed to the swaying city below.
As things return to normal, some land and walk away—continuing their conversations like nothing had happened—while others continue to swim forward through the air.
He recalls the Ægir rituals the people of Gran Faro had told him about when he was little.
Get up, Jordi.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: R-right!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Doña Irene?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Next time you go out, remember to put on the device that the Sea Patrol gave us when we landed yesterday.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Right, I remember that from the briefing videos... Which one was it again...?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: The fourth one. The technicians at the port reminded me.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: They make regular adjustments to the gravity settings, as part of what it takes to maintain the low-gravity environment of Milliarium.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: They said it's like a fin adjusting its swim bladder.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: So you went to tour the port.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Yes. I was interested in their ships and docks, their weapons... those massive ships that sail like fowlbeasts through reefs and cliffs.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I saw traces of the Stultifera Navis in them. Breogan really did recreate Ægir technology in Iberia. Perhaps...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Perhaps we should have sailed our proud armada out into the vast oceans, rather than parading our gold-gilded ships along the coasts as a deterrent to those dukes and pashas.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Breogan...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: You look nervous, Jordi. So nervous that you missed the point entirely.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'm just feeling a little out of place...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: This place is stranger than I imagined. The air is thick and heavy, the ocean above my head sends a chill up my spine, and the glowing plants along the streets make me dizzy.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Plus what happened just now...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Physical discomfort, I could deal with, but there are so many oddities here I can't even begin to understand yet.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The briefing videos Ægir provided were very detailed, but there's still so much that I couldn't comprehend, even after rewatching them so many times.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Food moves on its own without a fork. Clothes clean themselves without having to be removed. These things make sense, kind of.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But Edible Sagas? Crunchy Theorems? I just can't wrap my head around those. The best I can do for now is print out one of those emergency nutrition supply devices.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: All my life I've known nothing but Gran Faro. Is this what it's like to...?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: No, it's not quite like an Iberian from a backwater village seeing the capital for the first time. Not that the City of Gold still exists.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: The difference here isn't one between a small town and a metropolis, but... almost between two entirely different civilizations.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I tried to ask someone for directions, but couldn't understand what they were saying, or whether I was being rude to interrupt.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't even know how they see me—an Ægir in name only.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I have my concerns, too.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You're worried too?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: You of all people know what Iberia did to the Ægir after the Profound Silence.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I don't know what kind of country Ægir is, how its people view that period of bloodshed, or how they view me—an emissary with blood on her hands.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But you didn't—

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'm here representing the Iberian Inquisition. I've seen the files on the slaughters... Each report on its own may be thin, but in aggregate...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: We committed many injustices while cleansing the influence of the Church of the Deep, and the Islanders were the most affected.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I still believe the Inquisition was in no position to be lenient, not when the country itself teetered on the brink.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It was our collective decision that we should go to any lengths to ensure the nation's survival in a time of extraordinary crisis.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But that does not lessen our crime.
I don't believe you need worry about that.

steps.name: Haggard Scholar
steps.text: Growing a massive vesicle to resist a blast from Class III weaponry, and covering the retreat of the other Seaborn into the depths of the trench...

steps.name: Haggard Scholar
steps.text: How is it even possible for biological tissue to be made to resist the forces of a micro-singularity?

steps.name: Astute Officer
steps.text: The Sea Patrol brought back tissue samples. They've already been sent to your lab through the transport tubes.

steps.name: Haggard Scholar
steps.text: At least they haven't yet developed a collective resistance to Class III weaponry like they have for Classes I and II.

steps.name: Astute Officer
steps.text: The performance of Class III weaponry is demonstrably superior.

steps.name: Astute Officer
steps.text: But even more concerning is that an individual Seaborn has evolved measures specifically to counter it. They're more... organized than before.

steps.name: Astute Officer
steps.text: You've been analyzing the Seaborn's adaptation to various weaponry ever since Milliarium set sail. Did you already foresee this?

steps.name: Astute Officer
steps.text: Advisor Blandus?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: To an extent. But we need more time to confirm our theories.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Thank you, Secunda.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Your reports are always so detailed I dare not blink for fear of missing something. Little Handy, get me some eyedrops.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Ignore that command, Little Handy. Just a bad joke.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: If there's nothing else, I'll be going. I need to speak to the technicians about the damage suffered by our ships.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I'd rather you stay just a while longer, unless you're hurrying to get some rest after work.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Isn't it somewhat ironic, considering you've also received numerous health warnings but haven't seen a doctor yet?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: ...Very well. Still, I'd appreciate it if you could hear me out. It won't take long. I just need to confirm something—

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Have you read Gladiia's report?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I have.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Then you should know about Ulpianus. I thought you'd at least show some sort of reaction.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Of course I'm concerned about the reappearance of the Abyssal Hunters after five years of silence. Especially when the Waterway Program is at a key juncture.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: And Ulpianus's unusual activities are of particular note.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: He clearly made contact with Gladiia's group and is aware of Milliarium, but has made no attempt to reestablish communications with Ægir.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Meanwhile, we've heard from our Iberian sources that he's also declined to work with Iberia.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: He may be proud—arrogant even—but he is no fool. He must have his reasons for acting alone.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Regardless, I intend to find out where he is and what he's planning.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: That utilitarianism, that impatience... he's rubbed off on you. We had hoped you'd be better than that.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I can only pray your decision-making will be more prudent while tracking him.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Nevertheless, I have faith that you'll keep me updated on his whereabouts.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: What are you talking about, Advisor Blandus?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Neither of us is part of the Abyssal Hunter program anymore.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You're the weapons technology advisor for the Waterway Program now. Aren't utilitarian, impatient decisions the usual business in your field?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: And shouldn't you be getting information about Ulpianus from Milliarium's official sources? Why involve me?

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Just a momentary lapse in judgment. I can't fault you for carrying out your duty as Praefecta of the Sea Patrol.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: I just ask that you remember what Ulpianus did for us, for Ægir.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Yes, speaking.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: What? Missing?!

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'm on my way.

steps.name: Blandus
steps.text: Who's missing?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: One of the technicians on the Waterway Program has gone AWOL.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: And you are...?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Avitus, from the Institute of Prehistoric Studies, Academy of Science. We study the documents and artifacts of the prehistoric civilization.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Irene, emissary of the Iberian Inquisition.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Jordi. Jordi Fontanarossa.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: A pleasure to make your acquaintance.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: And don't worry, I didn't come to lecture you. I simply felt it was my duty as a citizen of Ægir to free our landbound friends from their needless concerns.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Needless concerns?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: What I mean to say is, Ægir understands that Iberia took measures proportionate to the extraordinary nature of the times.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: We can find similar periods in our own history, or even that of the glorious prehistoric civilization.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The exclusion of outsiders as a necessary means of maintaining social order appears to be an inevitable step in the progress of civilization.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Besides, we welcome our displaced countrymen to return to the sea, just as we respect the decision of those who have opted to leave.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The consequences of their choices belong only to them.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I appreciate Ægir's magnanimity, Avitus, but the 'consequences' they suffered were...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: No, it's nothing. Thank you for clarifying.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: You're welcome—

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: Mr. Avitus, our landbound guests, please be informed that this area has been designated for investigation.

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: You are advised to proceed to another area unless you have unresolved matters here.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: A Hand of the Saint?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: The Penal Battalion used them to clean up Seaborn remains, but I never knew they could talk.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Apparently, our people who brought them to land did not have time to demonstrate their full capabilities.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Multi-purpose Support Equipment, commonly known as a 'Little Handy.' They currently offer 972 different function modules, excluding obsolete ones.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: One can sometimes tell their affiliation just by looking at the parts and paintjob. This one, for example, belongs to the Sea Patrol.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Er, should I reply?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um, we're very sorry, Little Handy, er, sir.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: That would be unnecessary. It may be equipped with a voice, but that doesn't mean it's intelligent.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I assumed that with your technology, maybe...

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: It's true that the topic of simulated personalities has fascinated many a researcher.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The first attempt was created 230 years ago and continues to operate to this day. In fact, I can put in an application for you, if you wish to talk to it.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: However, whether from the perspective of neuroscience, psychology, sociology, or anthropology, simulated personalities have proven to be rather disappointing in terms of their benefits to research.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Perhaps I've gone off topic, though. In short, they've remained the stuff of niche research, and we do not consider them suitable for widespread application.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The goal of all technological development is to empower humanity. What purpose is there in turning a machine into a human?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I see. Fascinating.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: You said this Little Handy belonged to the Sea Patrol?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Only they would fit such powerful loudspeakers onto one, when quieter means of communication are available. I suppose you could consider it retro?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: What sort of organization are they? Do they frequently undertake such investigations?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The Sea Patrol is part of our Legions. They perform a supporting role in combat, as well as regular reconnaissance, patrol, security, and disaster response duties.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Emergency sweeps like this are rare, but with the Waterway Program at such a critical moment, it's only reasonable for them to be on high alert.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Little Handy, am I allowed to remain here?

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: It is not recommended, but not forbidden.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Then I'll wait here. I'd like a chance to speak to the Sea Patrol.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Very well. And you, Jordi?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll be going. Do you mind if I ask you some questions?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Of course not. There's a limit to what I can answer outside of my specialty, though.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Perhaps I could show you to a place better suited for such a conversation.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The Sophontheatrum.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Did you sleep well, Doctor? You seem a little haggard.

options: It's the air pressure. And humidity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes, the Ægir seem to have retained some of their aquatic traits.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Are you not feeling well?

options: Just a little short of breath.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is it serious?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let me know if you feel any discomfort.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Besides...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To be frank, I thought there may be another reason for your reaction.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Does anything about Ægir or the depths of the ocean seem familiar to you?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So you do remember something?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm accustomed to your usual silence, but now it's making me a little uneasy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know it might be difficult, but remembering even the slightest detail could be of great help to us all.

options: Sorry, I can't remember anything else.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's okay, just try to relax, Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Seeing the Preserver has inevitably hastened the pace at which you recall the truth... Even though I had hoped you would not touch upon what you'd forgotten so quickly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No one knows when your path of suffering will end. Not even yourself. In that, we are all powerless.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What we do know is that you've had an encounter with the abyss. The ocean is yet another path to your past, and we are finally upon it.

spans.text: know is that you've had an encounter with the abyss. The ocean is yet another path to your past, and we are finally upon it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes. I've wanted to set foot in Ægir countless times.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Until now, I have waited on the shore, and drifted on the waves.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have witnessed lighthouses and the armada turn from ideas to reality. Breogan had never given up on reestablishing communication with Ægir through such means.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But all his efforts ended in failure. Ægir never welcomed home their prodigal son, much less opened their doors to outsiders.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But now, they are even more eager to cooperate than I had anticipated. We need no longer waste efforts to persuade a proud and aloof giant.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can't deny feeling happy about that.

options: Is there something else troubling you?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm afraid there is.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ægir's proactive stance indicates that they have a plan for making contact with the land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But even the most moderate of their measures may seem too radical for landbound civilization. A single gesture of goodwill could cause a massive storm.

options: We should intervene as soon as possible.
The Abyssal Hunters are a good entry point.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Hunters' situation warrants concern, too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To Ægir, they are neither emissaries nor guests.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Having participated in the most radical project in Ægir's history, and 'come back to life' after being declared dead for five years... I worry that their return home would only cause—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Trouble?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Controversy?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Where's Gladiia?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: A somewhat troublesome fellow called her away.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I thought your priority upon returning would be to get checked up. What could possibly be more urgent?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No idea.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But once Gladiia's done with her interview, I guess Skadi and I are gonna go do some stupid check-up.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Swordfish and I are fine. Shark's changes might be a little problematic.

options: There's no Originium in the ocean, is there?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I read some medical papers before I underwent the surgery.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Even back then, they had advanced knowledge of medulla regeneration and replacement. They should be able to help her.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You needn't worry, Doctor.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I've inspected myself in the mirror on that great ship. On returning, those endless dreams still creep up on me like bubbles, but they've also become as light as bubbles.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Besides, I feel like I'd have more regrets about losing those dreams.

spans.text: Besides, I feel like I'd have more regrets about

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: But for now, I'm as lucid as I've ever been. And luckily for you, I'm even in the mood to take you on a tour of the city.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Interested?
